nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Project Memory (Booking & Appointment System)
nodes.rationale: Single project-memory file with two halves: (A) bootcamp/doc conventions, (B) booking-system domain logic. Read before any work so decisions and gotchas are not re-litigated.

nodes.label: User Entity (single entity + role field)
nodes.rationale: One User entity carrying a role field instead of a separate Provider entity — avoids duplicating identity/auth and lets a provider act as a consumer without a second account.

nodes.label: Role: CONSUMER
nodes.rationale: Browses services and books appointments; the only role with a dedicated /appointments page.

nodes.label: Role: PROVIDER
nodes.rationale: Offers one or more services via UserService N:M and self-manages personal availability including bulk generation. Built from the start, deliberately not deferred to future work.

nodes.label: Role: ADMIN
nodes.rationale: Full permissions: manage services, all users, all appointments, and bulk-generate availability for any provider.

nodes.label: UserService (provider↔service N:M)
nodes.rationale: N:M mapping so a provider can offer multiple services; owning side is User.services, which is what makes the Hibernate inverse-side staleness gotcha reachable.

nodes.label: AvailabilitySlot Entity
nodes.rationale: Belongs to a provider (a User with role PROVIDER), never to a service — the single decision the whole booking model rests on.

nodes.label: Service Entity (com.ammar.bookingsystem.service.Service)
nodes.rationale: Package/class name intentionally matches the domain/ERD rather than being renamed to dodge the Spring @Service annotation clash.

nodes.label: BookingService (booking logic bean)
nodes.rationale: Server-side authority for booking rules: rejects self-booking (400) before the DB, and owns updateStatus role/time/terminal-state gates.

nodes.label: BookingStatus (5 statuses)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED (initial) → CANCELLED / COMPLETED / NO_SHOW terminal states; VACANT exists as a Java enum value but is excluded by the V7 DB CHECK constraint so it can never be persisted.

nodes.label: AppSettings (single-row settings table)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a single-row table, not a generic key/value store: the admin's live booking horizon must survive restarts, apply immediately, and stay cheap to cache in memory.

nodes.label: GoogleAccountConnection Entity
nodes.rationale: Per-provider Google OAuth link with an encrypted refresh token; a provider is not bookable until connected.

nodes.label: Core Rule: Appointments Bound to Provider Availability
nodes.rationale: If slots hung off services, a provider offering 5 services with 5 daily slots would falsely advertise 25 bookable appointments. Binding slots to the provider keeps the real capacity honest.

nodes.label: Rule: Booking One Service Reserves the Slot Across All That Provider's Services
nodes.rationale: Direct consequence of slots belonging to the provider: one human cannot be in two appointments at once, so the reservation must be visible from every service they offer.

nodes.label: Rule: Provider May Book Others, Never Their Own Availability
nodes.rationale: Enforced twice — the day view filters the provider's own entry client-side, and BookingService rejects it with 400 server-side before it reaches the DB. The client filter is explicitly not trusted.

nodes.label: Stacked Provider Dropdowns (day-view slot browsing)
nodes.rationale: Chosen option 2 (provider-preferred times): each provider is a dropdown and several can be open at once so the consumer can compare, and the list scrolls as provider count grows.

nodes.label: Booking Horizon (admin-configurable, default 6 months)
nodes.rationale: Default in application.yaml (booking.max-horizon-months: 6) via @ConfigurationProperties; live admin value in AppSettings. Enforced in two places — calendar UI and server-side booking validation.

nodes.label: Provider Advance Limit (ceil(horizon × multiplier), default 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Providers/admins must pre-load availability further ahead than consumers can book (9 months at horizon 6). Multiplier is yaml-only, not admin-facing; the window rolls so pre-loaded slots become bookable over time.

nodes.label: Calendar Navigation Constrained to the Booking Window
nodes.rationale: Year picker lists only the 1–2 years the window spans; the 12-month grid shadows months before today and beyond the horizon; past days are non-selectable and non-navigable.

nodes.label: Calendar Pressure Coloring (available/total per day)
nodes.rationale: ≥4 available = low pressure (green/lighter), 3 = medium (yellow), 1–2 = about to run out (warm/alert), 0 = shadowed. Colors derived from the site palette so pressure signalling never disrupts the brand.

nodes.label: Rule: Weekends Are Not Special — Shadowing Follows Slot Availability Only
nodes.rationale: A Fri/Sat with provider slots renders by its pressure; a weekday with none is shadowed. A provider may legitimately choose to work weekends, so the calendar must not hardcode a weekend concept.

nodes.label: All Slots Render; Booked Ones Styled Distinctly
nodes.rationale: Showing booked slots shadowed (rather than hiding them) tells the consumer appointments existed on that date but are taken, which reads as a fuller, more trustworthy schedule.

nodes.label: Booking Confirmation UX (enabled button + success toast)
nodes.rationale: Button looks disabled until a slot is selected; on success a corner toast auto-dismisses after ~30s with an 'x' to close early, naming service, date, time and confirming the email was sent.

nodes.label: Booking Status Lifecycle & Gates
nodes.rationale: CANCELLED only >24h before start and frees the slot back to AVAILABLE; COMPLETED only after slot end (provider/admin); NO_SHOW only after end and leaves the slot BOOKED; terminal states are final → 409.

nodes.label: VACANT Is Synthesized, Never Persisted
nodes.rationale: A dashboard-only label for open AVAILABLE slots, emitted with a negative id (=-slotId) and null consumer. The V7 DB CHECK constraint deliberately excludes it so code cannot write it even though it is a Java enum value.

nodes.label: PATCH /api/bookings/{id}/status
nodes.rationale: Single transition entry point into BookingService.updateStatus; the server is the real gate while the modal only shadows disallowed buttons.

nodes.label: Landing Page (public)
nodes.rationale: Hero → How-it-works/journey → Services preview → optional FAQ → Footer (research R3). Deliberately no social-proof section — an MVP has no proof to show.

nodes.label: Booking Page (public service browse)
nodes.rationale: Browsing is open to anonymous users; attempting to book prompts sign-in/sign-up and then redirects back to the exact flow the user was on.

nodes.label: Calendar / Slot Selection Page (/book/[serviceId])
nodes.rationale: A dedicated page rather than a modal (research R4) — supports a multi-step flow, a shareable URL, and a clean auth-redirect back into the flow.

nodes.label: Shared Dashboard (/dashboard — provider + admin)
nodes.rationale: Same UI for both roles (research R2); admins get the extra provider filter. Providers see only their own data plus their own consumer-side bookings.

nodes.label: My Appointments (/appointments — consumer-only)
nodes.rationale: Nav link hidden and direct navigation redirects providers/admins to /dashboard. Backed by GET /api/bookings?mine=true, self-scoped server-side — the client is never trusted for scoping.

nodes.label: "(You)" Merge for Viewer-as-Consumer Rows
nodes.rationale: Providers/admins get no separate 'my bookings' page; their own consumer-side bookings merge into /dashboard with the name bolded and a trailing '(You)' so the row does not read as a real patient.

nodes.label: AppointmentDetailsModal (shared, both tables)
nodes.rationale: Every row in both appointment tables opens it; it is the only place the meeting link is shown, and it shows role-appropriate status buttons while shadowing disallowed ones with an explanatory note.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay (blurred full-page wait)
nodes.rationale: The Book button triggers a synchronous Google Calendar + email round-trip slow enough to feel broken. Content stays visible under the blur (never disappears); the confirmation toast is carried across the redirect via query params, cleared immediately so a refresh doesn't re-show it.

nodes.label: Bulk Availability Generator (weekdays × date range × time ranges)
nodes.rationale: Available to providers for their own slots and to admins for any provider — entering slots one by one would make the system unusable.

nodes.label: /dashboard/connect-google
nodes.rationale: Shows which Google account is connected — the reason the userinfo.email scope was added beyond the original spec.

nodes.label: Shared Dashboard Filter System
nodes.rationale: Service / Status / Provider (admin-only) multi-selects plus a date-range picker defaulting to today, applied to every section of the page rather than per-widget.

nodes.label: Stat Cards (4, date-range-driven)
nodes.rationale: Narrowed by service+provider but deliberately NOT by the status filter — each card has an intrinsic status meaning (a no-show rate needs completed+no_show regardless of what the user filtered).

nodes.label: "Bookings over time" Chart + Month/Week/Day Toggle
nodes.rationale: Chart and calendar share one granularity toggle anchored at the range start; calendar month is a real 42-cell (6×7) calendar-aligned grid, not a flat day list.

nodes.label: GET /api/bookings/{feed,stats,chart}
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated serviceIds/statuses/providerIds plus from/to. feed returns real bookings plus synthesized VACANT entries, excluded when a specific service is filtered and only when VACANT is among selected statuses.

nodes.label: Confirmation Email via Gmail SMTP
nodes.rationale: Sent to BOTH parties on every booking — consumer confirmation plus a separate provider notification naming the consumer, so the provider learns of a new appointment without checking the dashboard.

nodes.label: Google Meet Links via Google Calendar API
nodes.rationale: events.insert with conferenceDataVersion=1 + conferenceData.createRequest + hangoutsMeet under OAuth2. Feasible on a free Gmail (Workspace only needed for the Admin SDK path); the link comes back as a plain string so the custom UI is preserved.

nodes.label: Per-Provider Google OAuth Connection
nodes.rationale: Each provider connects their own account once (scopes calendar.events + userinfo.email; refresh token stored encrypted). The event lands on the provider's calendar with attendees=[consumer, provider] and sendUpdates=all so the provider is host and guests join directly with no manual admit.

nodes.label: Fallback: Provider-Pasted Persistent Meet Link
nodes.rationale: A provider is not bookable until connected, so a manual persistent personal Meet link keeps the system usable when OAuth cannot be completed.

nodes.label: RBAC — Spring Security Filter Chain + Method-Level Authorization
nodes.rationale: Baseline pattern from common_blueprints.md §1. Security review is an explicit step: attempt unauthorized page/action access and confirm it is blocked.

nodes.label: JWT Bearer Auth (security/ package)
nodes.rationale: JwtService, JwtAuthenticationFilter, AppUserDetailsService, UserPrincipal, CurrentUser. Only /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login are public — never permitAll the whole /api/auth/** because /me must require authentication.

nodes.label: common_blueprints.md §1 (RBAC baseline)
nodes.rationale: External blueprint cited as the RBAC baseline pattern for this project.

nodes.label: Backend: Spring Boot 4.1.0 + Spring Data JPA (JVM 21)
nodes.rationale: Initializr default; docs originally said '3'. ddl-auto: validate — Flyway owns the schema and Hibernate only checks entities match it.

nodes.label: Flyway Schema Migrations (db/migration/)
nodes.rationale: Flyway is the schema owner; V7 carries the BookingStatus CHECK constraint that excludes VACANT.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL — Native Windows PG16 Service for Local Dev
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a Docker container after U3 hit a port-5432 conflict with an existing docker-less local Postgres. DB booking_system, user bookingadmin owns the DB so it owns public schema on PG15+ without extra grants. Production still targets managed/containerized Postgres.

nodes.label: spring-dotenv (springboot4-dotenv) for Dev Credentials
nodes.rationale: Loads app/backend/.env (git-ignored) in dev while real env vars still take precedence, so the same config stays safe in production. .env.example is committed with placeholders only.

nodes.label: Frontend: Next.js 16 App Router + React 19 + Tailwind v4
nodes.rationale: create-next-app default (docs originally said '14'), src/ layout in app/frontend. AGENTS.md warns this Next.js has breaking changes vs training data — check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing page code.

nodes.label: Design System (src/components/ds, via Claude Design + DesignSync)
nodes.rationale: Importable as @/components/ds; ds/screens-reference/ holds visual references only, never imported code.

nodes.label: lib/api.ts api() Helper
nodes.rationale: Checks response text before JSON.parse regardless of status code (not just 204), because a 200 with an empty body from a void controller method would otherwise throw on res.json().

nodes.label: UI Libraries: Framer Motion, Embla Carousel, Lucide React
Gotcha: Flyway Needs spring-boot-starter-flyway on Boot 4
nodes.rationale: FlywayAutoConfiguration moved into its own module — bare flyway-core + flyway-database-postgresql does NOT trigger it and fails SILENTLY: no error, Flyway never runs, DB stays empty. Keep flyway-database-postgresql explicit since it is optional inside the starter.

nodes.label: Convention: @Component, Never @Service
nodes.rationale: Any class importing the Service entity cannot also import org.springframework.stereotype.Service under its simple name. Using @Component everywhere sidesteps the clash uniformly instead of fully-qualifying case by case.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Jackson 3 Relocation (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: Importing com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper compiles fine but throws NoClassDefFoundError at runtime. Spring MVC's own JSON is unaffected; prefer avoiding a direct Jackson dependency in low-level beans like security filters.

nodes.label: Gotcha: SecurityConfig Needs Explicit .exceptionHandling(...)
nodes.rationale: Without an AuthenticationEntryPoint, an unauthenticated/forbidden request surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of 401/403.

nodes.label: Gotcha: @PreAuthorize Denials Need Their Own @ExceptionHandler
nodes.rationale: Method-security AOP throws AccessDeniedException INSIDE the MVC handler invocation, so it never reaches SecurityConfig's filter-level accessDeniedHandler; without a dedicated handler in GlobalExceptionHandler it falls into the blanket Exception catch-all as a 500 instead of 403.

nodes.label: Gotcha: void @DeleteMapping Returns 200 + Empty Body, Not 204
nodes.rationale: Return ResponseEntity.noContent().build() explicitly — an empty-but-200 response breaks naive frontend clients that call res.json() unconditionally on success.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Hibernate L1 Cache + Inverse-Side @ManyToMany Staleness
nodes.rationale: Mutating the owning side (User.services) then re-fetching the inverse side's owner (Service) in the same persistence context returns the already-loaded instance with a stale lazy collection. Build the response from data you already know is correct instead of re-querying.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Google OAuth Callback Params Must Be Optional
nodes.rationale: The 'user clicked Cancel' redirect sends error=access_denied with NO code param. Required @RequestParams turn the most common non-happy path into MissingServletRequestParameterException (raw 500). Make them required=false and check for a Google error param before the token exchange.

nodes.label: Pattern: OAuth state as a Signed, Purpose-Tagged JWT
nodes.rationale: Google's callback is a plain browser redirect with no Authorization header, so the initiating provider's user id travels in a short-lived (10 min) signed token reusing the existing JWT key — the only way a public callback endpoint can know which provider it is for.

nodes.label: Gotcha: spring.mail Nested Properties Need Bracket-Quoted YAML Keys
nodes.rationale: Write "[mail.smtp.ssl.enable]": true, not nested YAML maps. Gmail SMTP on port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS — ssl.enable is what matters, not starttls.enable.

nodes.label: Gotcha: DS Components with Hooks Need "use client"
nodes.rationale: Accordion.jsx used React.useState without "use client" and threw 'useState is not a function' at build time when rendered from a Server Component. Check any newly-pulled DS component for internal hook usage.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Public DB-Backed Pages Need force-dynamic
nodes.rationale: Without export const dynamic = "force-dynamic", Next statically bakes the fetch result in at build time and the services preview goes stale.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Avoid Native number/date/time Inputs (OS-locale rendering)
nodes.rationale: Chromium renders these using the OS locale — on an Arabic machine this produced Arabic-Indic digits and Arabic day/month/hour labels. Use type="text" with YYYY-MM-DD / HH:MM placeholders and regex validation; values stay plain strings either way.

nodes.label: Gotcha: toLocaleDateString(undefined, ...) Uses the Browser/OS Locale
nodes.rationale: Caught rendering Arabic month names on a test machine with an Arabic locale. Always pass an explicit locale ("en-US") until real i18n is wired up.

nodes.label: Context Protocol — conversation_history.md as Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: All prompts and full responses live there and the chat stays a minimal pointer; raw prompts are reformatted to clean Markdown with nothing removed, in numbered '§ N — Response to Prompt #M' sections.

nodes.label: Global Rule: requirements-standards.md (EARS, flat IDs, Gherkin)
Global Rule: i18n-directionality.md (RTL/LTR + logical properties)
nodes.rationale: Created in Phase 0; paths:-scoped in the trainee package so it only fires on UI files.

nodes.label: PROJECT_REPORT.md (single graded report)
nodes.rationale: Per section: brief instructions → template → short generic example → actual booking-system data. An extraction source for the curriculum, never named inside it.

nodes.label: implementation_plan.md (granular coding plan)
nodes.rationale: Requirements → acceptance criteria.

nodes.label: research_plan.md (research spikes R1–R4)
nodes.rationale: R1 = Google Meet feasibility, R2 = dashboard design, R3 = landing sections, R4 = dedicated page vs modal. Each cited design decision traces back to one of these spikes.

nodes.label: bootcamp_roadmap_and_curriculum.md (Arabic curriculum)
nodes.rationale: Must stay identical for every trainee (it is the deck's source). Ground every section in the real sources, never memory; never name internal/graded docs inside it.

nodes.label: Trainee Package Architecture — Four Non-Overlapping Surfaces
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md = identity/progress (always loaded); rules/*.md = always-on behavior (kept short since loaded in full every message); skills/<name>/SKILL.md = on-demand per-section playbooks (only the description sits in context, which is what keeps per-message cost flat); roadmap + PRODUCT.md = the only trainee-read files. Template prompts are deliberately duplicated between skill and trainee material — belt and braces, do not deduplicate.

nodes.label: Curriculum's Generic Default Stack (Next.js + Supabase + Vercel)
nodes.rationale: Full-stack Next.js in one app/ folder with no frontend/backend split, Supabase for Postgres + built-in auth (no Docker/local install), deploy to Vercel; Claude scaffolds everything and the trainee only creates accounts/keys. The booking project's heavier real stack stays trainer-example-only inside collapsibles.

nodes.label: Principle: Trainee Never Reads/Writes Code; Testing Is Claude's Job
nodes.rationale: The trainee reviews by using the UI plus Claude's plain report; Claude writes and runs test cases and browser tests automatically on every build. Plans open with a plain-language 'what we'll build now' summary before any technical detail.

nodes.label: Rule: Register Every New Tool in Both Places
nodes.rationale: Any new tool/MCP/skill must be added to this file's 'Tools available' list AND the curriculum's Section 17 table (plus its booking collapsible if booking-specific), so nothing is missed on review. The Tools Used table is the most-requested doc section.

nodes.label: Convention: Plan Mode Before Any Coding Task
nodes.rationale: Review, then execute — never execute a coding task straight from the prompt.

nodes.label: Tool: context7 (MCP) — up-to-date library docs
nodes.rationale: Used whenever writing code so generated code matches current APIs rather than training data.

nodes.label: Tool: Claude Design + DesignSync
nodes.rationale: Component library pulled one component at a time into src/components/ds rather than a wholesale replace.

nodes.label: Tool: Vercel MCP (deploy management + logs)
nodes.rationale: Must be connected before deploying so failures are diagnosed from real logs instead of guessed.

nodes.label: Tool: Supabase MCP (curriculum default stack only)
nodes.rationale: OAuth, no PAT. Explicitly NOT used by the booking build itself — it belongs to the trainee default stack.

nodes.label: Monorepo Layout (app/backend + app/frontend, docs at root)
nodes.rationale: github.com/AmmarDw/booking-system.git. Build is compressed to ~2 real days though the docs narrate the official 6.
